disclaimer: Fair-price ranges are estimates compiled from metered fares, official entry-fee schedules, TAAN/porter-welfare guidance and recent traveler reports. Ranges move with seasons and negotiation — use them as a sanity check, not a fixed rate.

universal.taxiNotes: Metered taxis in Kathmandu run around Rs 80 per km; most drivers refuse the meter for tourists. Always agree the price before getting in. Night rides (10 pm–6 am) run ~50% higher. In Pokhara, Pathao/InDrive show the fare in advance and are the safest option.
universal.busNotes: Local green buses are cheapest but crowded; tourist coaches (Greenline, Mountain Overland) cost more and are safer. Avoid riding on roofs and travelling after dark.
universal.entryNote: Most heritage sites charge a lower 'SAARC' or 'Nepali' rate and a higher foreign-tourist rate. Ask for the official ticket booth and keep your ticket for spot checks.

scams.title: Taxi 'broken meter' overcharge
scams.script: Driver claims the meter is broken and quotes 2–4× the fair rate (e.g. Rs 1,000 for a ride that should cost Rs 300).
redFlags: Quote far above what you expect
Driver insists on a 'friendly detour' or 'no change' at the end
scams.response: Politely refuse, step out, and use Pathao/InDrive, or walk 100 m to the next taxi. Agree the price in writing before boarding.
scams.phrase: कृपया मिटर अन गर्नुहोस् — Please turn on the meter

scams.title: 'Free' guide who expects payment
scams.script: A friendly local 'guides' you around a durbar square or temple for free, then demands a large tip or steers you to commission shops.
redFlags: Leads you to gem, thangka or carpet shops
scams.response: Smile, say 'no thank you' firmly and walk away. If you want a guide, hire a licensed one from the official desk.
scams.phrase: धन्यवाद, मलाई गाइड चाहिँदैन — Thanks, I don't need a guide

scams.title: Fake trekking agency or unlicensed guide
scams.script: Hired via Facebook, TripAdvisor or a street tout. No registered agency, no insurance, sometimes no real permit. Linked to several 2025 missing-trekker cases.
redFlags: No TAAN/NMA registration or license number
Won't put the itinerary and cost in writing
Guide can't show insurance or TIMS permit
scams.response: Book only through a TAAN-registered agency and verify the guide's license. If it's already too late, report it and switch agencies.
scams.phrase: तपाईंको दर्ता नम्बर के हो? — What is your registration number?

scams.title: Helicopter 'rescue' scam
scams.script: A guide/operator pressures a mildly-altitude-sick trekker into a costly helicopter medevac, then splits the inflated bill with the hospital.
redFlags: Pressure to evacuate before medical confirmation
Asking you to hand over your insurance documents
scams.response: Rest a day first and call your insurer directly before approving any evacuation. Only use TAAN-registered agencies.
scams.phrase: म पहिले मेरो बीमा कम्पनीलाई सम्पर्क गर्छु — I'll contact my insurance company first

scams.title: Shop pressure & fake souvenirs
scams.script: 'Yak wool' that is acrylic, fake pashmina, mass-printed 'antique' thangkas, and commission-loaded 'friend's shop' stops.
redFlags: No price tag or a 'special price for you'
Tour guide earns commission from your purchase
scams.response: Buy from fixed-price stores or cooperatives, look for the 'Chyangra Pashmina' label, and compare 3 shops before buying.
scams.phrase: यो महँगो छ, घटाउनुहोस् — This is expensive, reduce it

scams.title: Begging & 'orphanage' milk-powder con
scams.script: Vendors or people ask tourists to buy overpriced milk powder 'for orphans', which is returned to the shop for cash. Fake charities collect 'donations'.
redFlags: Pressure to buy a specific product for 'charity'
Charity has no registration you can verify
scams.response: Donate only to registered NGOs with verifiable records, never to street collectors.

scams.title: Bar & club hidden fees
scams.script: No menu or a menu with no prices; 'service fees' and 'entertainment fees' appear on the bill.
scams.response: Ask to see prices before ordering and check the bill line by line.
scams.phrase: मेनुमा मूल्य देखाउनुहोस् — Show me the prices on the menu

scams.title: Money-changer counterfeit switch
scams.script: A 'helpful' exchanger swaps your notes and hands back counterfeit or short-changed currency.
redFlags: Handling your money out of sight
scams.response: Use banks or licensed exchange counters only, and count notes before leaving.
scams.phrase: म बैंकमा गर्छु — I'll do it at the bank

scams.title: Bus ticket double-charge
scams.script: On some routes (e.g. Besishahar–Pokhara) a second operator demands payment again, claiming the fare didn't cover their leg.
redFlags: Second driver asks you to pay the same amount twice
scams.response: Insist on a printed ticket for the whole journey and refuse to pay twice; call tourist police if threatened.
scams.phrase: मैले पहिले नै तिरिसकेको छु — I have already paid

entryFees.note: Non-Hindus can view from the far bank

shoppingSanity.check: Never above Rs 60 in the city

scamCards.title: Airport taxi overcharge
scamCards.script: Exit-arrivals touts quote Rs 1,500+ for the Rs 500–700 airport–Thamel ride.
scamCards.response: Walk to the road and use a metered taxi or Pathao.

scamCards.title: Pashupatinath 'free' guide
scamCards.script: Pushy 'guides' ambush visitors at the main gate and demand money after the tour.
scamCards.response: Say no at the gate and walk in.

shoppingSanity.check: Lakeside prices are inflated for tourists

scamCards.title: Airport 'broken meter' taxi
scamCards.script: The classic: 'meter is broken, Rs 1,000 to Lakeside'. Real fare is Rs 300–400.
scamCards.response: Book via your guesthouse or use InDrive/Pathao; walk past the kerbside cluster.

scamCards.title: Paragliding 'special' upsell
scamCards.script: Operators quote high 'peak season' prices; official drop zone rates are published.
scamCards.response: Ask for the published rate and book through a licensed operator.

entryFees.note: Per group; price varies by season

scamCards.title: Bogus 'safari package' agencies
scamCards.script: Unaffiliated agents sell 'guaranteed tiger sighting' packages at inflated prices.
scamCards.response: Book through the lodge you stay at or a TAAN-registered agency.

entryFees.note: Requires an approved trekking agency; extra $50 per extra day

scamCards.title: Restricted-area permit confusion
scamCards.script: Touts sell 'fast-track' permits for Upper Mustang at inflated fees.
redFlags: Permit cost far above the official $500/10-day rate
scamCards.response: Permits must go through an approved agency; verify the official fee.

entryFees.note: One-way; book early in peak season

mealBands.note: Tea-house dal bhat is the value option

scamCards.title: Helicopter 'evacuation' scare
scamCards.script: Pressure to take a medevac heli for mild AMS, then inflated bills billed to insurers.
scamCards.response: Rest, hydrate, call your insurer directly before deciding.

scamCards.title: Unlicensed guide at Lukla
scamCards.script: Directly hired guides at Lukla often have no registered agency — linked to missing-trekker cases.
scamCards.response: Book through a registered agency in Kathmandu.

mealBands.note: Tea-house food gets pricier with altitude

shoppingSanity.check: Buy from tea gardens or cooperatives

entryFees.note: Restricted areas need permits via agencies
